lines.text: Do you know how a secret ballot works? It's built so nobody can ever prove how you voted. Not even you.
For centuries, votes were often called out loud, or cast on coloured party tickets everyone could see. Bosses and bribers watched.
In 1856, the colony of Victoria in Australia tried something new. One official paper, listing every candidate, printed by the government.
You mark it alone behind a screen, fold it, and drop it in a sealed box. Your name is never written on it.
When polls close, the box is opened in front of watchers from every side, and the papers are counted.
Since no one can check your vote, buying it is pointless. That's the whole trick.
Britain adopted it in 1872, and today almost every democracy uses it.
Orbi's Anonymous mode keeps the same spirit. No profile, no name, no GPS. Just a throwaway ID that's gone when you leave.
